note: GOOGLE SIGN-UP CREATED A USER WHO BELONGED TO NO CHURCH. A real member of kingdom-living.theharvest.app ended up with a `users` document carrying `tenantId: null` — signed in, and signed in to nothing: no CRM row, no dashboard row, no prayer request, no posts, because `set-custom-claims.ts` mints the `tenantId` claim from that very field and `firestore.rules` gates every piece of tenant content on the claim. The brief's hypothesis was an iOS redirect hop; it is FALSIFIED and the falsification is asserted, not argued — `signInWithRedirect` and `getRedirectResult` appear in no source file in `src/`, the product uses `signInWithPopup`, which navigates a separate window and never moves the opener's hostname, and a measured run of the real screen on `kingdom-living.theharvest.app` writes `kingdom-living` on both the Google and the email path. The defect that IS real and IS reproducible is `tenantId: <x> || null` on three create paths: that operator cannot tell 'belongs to no ministry' — a super admin, the apex, the www/app/admin/affiliate aliases, a `*.vercel.app` preview, where null is CORRECT and is untouched by this ticket — from 'belongs to a ministry and I could not name it', and writes null for both. The host where the second one bites is a CUSTOM DOMAIN: `AuthPage`'s fallback there is a `tenantId=` cookie described as 'set server-side by middleware via resolve-domain', and `src/middleware.ts` only rate-limits `/api/*` and sets no cookie at all — `lib/custom-domain-feature.ts` had already recorded the same finding about `api/resolve-domain`. A second divergence was closed on the way: `AuthPage` alone accepted `*.vercel.app` and stamped a preview's first label as a tenant slug while every other resolver said null, so a signup on a preview URL was written into a ministry that never existed. THE-349 records NO firestore.rules digest and that is the posture of the ticket rather than an omission: the repair a stuck member needs is a `tenantId` write, and the `users` update rule refuses one to the member AND to their tenant admin (`tenantId` is in the self-edit blocklist and immutable on the admin branch) — only `isSuperAdmin()` or the Admin SDK can make it, so the repair is REPORTED as a Firebase console change for the founder and the rule is asserted as it stands. firestore.indexes.json, functions/, src/app/layout.tsx, package.json and package-lock.json are untouched and asserted as such; no npm dependency, no theme token and no new primitive was installed — the refusal composes `ui/alert`, which was already on disk. One file this ticket edits is deliberately NOT recorded here: the shared rules-digest register's own suite, whose PINNING_SUITES count is bumped in step with the ownership register's. Its path carries a ticket number that is itself a record in this directory, and the no-index guard forbids naming one record from another in a structural field - so recording it would be an index by another name. The append there is a one-line count and a per-ticket note beside the existing ones, exactly as the ticket before this one left it.

entries.why: THE-349 OWNS this file and this is the state it leaves it in. Four changes. (1) The tenant is a THREE-way answer, not a `string | null`: `resolveAuthTenant()` returns `tenant` / `platform` / `unresolved`, and `unresolved` is the answer nothing may write. (2) Both creates go through `tenantIdToWrite()`, which returns the slug for `tenant`, null for `platform` and THROWS for `unresolved` — so the line cannot regress into `|| null` by itself, and the gates above it are what keep it from ever being asked. (3) The refusal lands BEFORE Firebase on both signup paths, so no Auth user and no `users` doc exist to clean up, and at the create branch on the sign-in path too, because a first-time member arrives through the sign-in view by default and that branch is the only one that can orphan anybody — an EXISTING member on a custom domain is untouched and still signs in, which is measured. (4) The generic 'Unable to sign in. Please try again.' is replaced by messages named per cause: `auth/account-exists-with-different-credential` (the reported member's own collision — Google first, then a password account on the same address, after which every Google press fails identically), `auth/unauthorized-domain`, `auth/popup-blocked`, `auth/user-disabled`, `auth/too-many-requests` and `auth/invalid-credential`, which v10 uses for BOTH a wrong password and an unknown address and was therefore the single largest consumer of a retry that could not help; the generic line survives only for a genuine unknown, where trying again is real advice. Also: the screen now refuses to call `signInWithPopup` inside an iPhone home-screen app, because `@firebase/auth`'s `_open()` hands the URL to Safari when `_isIOSStandalone` and returns `new AuthPopup(null)`, whose close-poller reads `undefined` forever — the promise never settles, no catch can speak, and the button spins until the app is killed. That is 'it kicked him out', and this product's own onboarding asks iPhone members to install exactly that home-screen app. The tenant derivation moved from an effect to a lazy initialiser so it is never null for a first render. The state derived from it, `tenantId`, still reads null for `platform` at the member-cap pre-flight, so D7's 'no tenant, no cap applies' is unchanged and measured.

THE-349 OWNS this file and this is the state it leaves it in. `writeUserDoc`'s CREATE branch — THE-336's safety net for a member whose `AuthPage` create was refused — carried the same `tenantId: tenantId || null` off `getTenantScope()`, so fixing only `AuthPage` would have moved the orphan here rather than removed it. `resolveCreateTenant()` still asks `getTenantScope()` FIRST and unchanged: the host, then the super-admin fallback, then the member's own document, in that order, and every answer it can give it still gives. What changed is what its NULL is taken to mean — the host classifier is asked only to tell 'legitimately no ministry' from 'could not name one', and a super admin on such a host is `platform` and still writes null, unrefused, because refusing them would break the very thing this ticket's non-negotiables name. An unresolved create throws with a code `saveFailureMessage` maps to copy that names a next step rather than 'something went wrong saving your answers', which would be false: nothing went wrong with the save. THE-336's shape is otherwise intact and re-measured — the create still happens instead of rejecting with `not-found` (the #479 bug that stopped ALL signups), the UPDATE branch still carries the caller's fields ONLY because the rule refuses a self-edit touching `role` or `tenantId`, and the update branch is never refused whatever the host, so a member who already belongs to a ministry can always save their own answers. One stale sentence in THE-336's docblock is corrected in place: it said this file resolves off a tenant host to null 'exactly as AuthPage does when the middleware cookie is absent', which described the bug rather than the behaviour.

THE-349 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-348 owned the one before it and THE-346 the one before that. `RULES_PINNERS_NOW` goes 65 -> 66 and this ticket's guard suite joins `RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE` beside THE-348's entry, never over it — the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-349 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere: it FOUND that the fix must not touch the rules — the repair a stuck member needs is a `tenantId` write, which the `users` update rule refuses to the member and to their tenant admin alike, so loosening it would open a tenant-hopping surface in a file that auto-deploys on merge with no emulator tests — and reports the repair as a Firebase console change for the founder while ASSERTING the rule as it stands, so the suite goes red the day the rule moves and the repair instructions become stale.

THE-349 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-339 and THE-345 owned the ones before it. `src/components/AuthPage.tsx` joins RECORDED_ADOPTERS as an adopter of `alert`, with the rejections of `sonner`, `dialog` and `empty` named per element, because the guard refuses ANY importer of a batch C/D/E primitive that is not on the list - which is the whole point of the list and is why this file had to be opened rather than worked around. No recorded adopter is removed, no reason is shortened, and the three runtime packages (cmdk, react-day-picker, react-resizable-panels) are untouched: `alert` pulls none of them, so this PR's bundle consequence is still zero. The entry also records what was deliberately NOT adopted - the two hand-rolled message boxes already on the auth screen are left exactly as they were, because converting working copy this ticket does not own would be a visual pass smuggled in behind a data fix.
